q: In the promo-apr-test project, what do we know about pa-margin-v2?
a: The 24-month net margin model that adds post-expiry churn hazard and expected loss by score band to pa-margin-v1. Arm B against control is +$38 per account over 24 months overall and -$72 in the under-640 band; it superseded pa-margin-v1.

q: In the promo-apr-test project, what came of exp-505-exit-churn?
a: Arm C accounts churned at 6.4% in 60 days after promo expiry, against 2.1% for control. That became find-pa-cliff-churn, which led to dec-pa-glide-exit: a glide-path exit from 0% to 12% over three months, to be tested in November 2026.

q: In the promo-apr-test project, what does pa-margin-v2 depend on?
a: pa-bal-forecast-v1 for balance paths to month 24, pa-churn-hazard-v1 for post-expiry churn, feat-pa-bt-inflow-v2 for external BT inflow, and feat-pa-credit-band for the score-band loss term.

q: In the promo-apr-test project, what is the current default promo structure for new accounts?
a: A 6-month 0% promo is the default (dec-pa-6m-default, 2026-10-14). The 12-month promo is kept only for scores 640-699, and is not offered below 640 (dec-pa-no-12m-subprime).

q: In the promo-apr-test project, what was arm C's BT inflow in months 1-3 relative to arm B, on the v1 basis?
a: $980 against $1,420 per account, i.e. 69% of the 12-month arm's lift (exp-502, built on exp-501); both are before the intra-bank fix.

q: In the promo-apr-test project, why is the default promo now 6 months at 0%?
a: The 6-month arm keeps 69% of the 12-month BT lift at lower exposure (find-pa-6m-arm), and the 12-month promo loses money below 640 once churn and loss are counted (find-pa-margin-corrected), with its response concentrated in the 640-699 band (find-pa-band-het). So dec-pa-6m-default made 6 months the default and kept 12 months only for 640-699.
